papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.desc: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) represent model activations with sparse, linearly decoded features, but the downstream effects of those features need not compose additively.

papers.title: Beyond Policy Rollouts: Embedding-Space Directional Exploration with Anchored Noise for LLM RLVR
papers.desc: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically uses small rollout groups per prompt, where repeated sampling from the same policy can yield highly similar trajectories, reducing within-group reward variation and weakening group-relative advantage signals.

papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.desc: Computer-use agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks, where running a frontier model at every step is expensive and a small open-weight model alone often fails.

papers.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
papers.desc: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video.

papers.title: Mine, Sample, Render: Test-Time Diversity Alignment Of Generative Models
papers.desc: Modern generative models produce high-quality individual outputs but struggle to sample diversely, even when explicitly instructed to do so.

papers.title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
papers.desc: AI systems now write long and difficult mathematical proofs, and checking their step-by-step validity is becoming a bottleneck.

papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.desc: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs.

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.desc: Agent environments are essential for large language model (LLM) development.

papers.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
papers.desc: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting.

papers.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
papers.desc: When does a language model acquire a capability? Developmental studies usually answer this by tracking when models start producing the correct token.

papers.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
papers.desc: Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it.

papers.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR
papers.desc: Character Error Rate (CER), the standard metric for OCR and vision-language models (VLMs), charges a typo as much as a wrong name.

papers.title: One Bias Score, Two Factors: How Mitigations Affect Option Bias in Multiple-Choice Evaluation
papers.desc: Reordering multiple-choice options can change a model's answer, an effect studied as selection bias (a preference for certain option letters) and as order sensitivity (changes in answers across option orderings).

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
papers.desc: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are typically trained on hundreds of millions to billions of activation tokens, yet little work has tested whether this scale is necessary.

papers.title: PAIR: Bridging Perception and Action in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.desc: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map visual observations and language instructions to continuous robot actions.
